newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY RADIO NOON HEADLINES - OCT 10.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY RADIO NOON HEADLINES - OCT 10.

text.p: These are the main headlines on Hungary's Kossuth Radio midday news. Reuters cannot vouch for their accuracy:

- Tocsik Marta, a consultant in focus of the privatisation scandal, did not attend the second day of hearings in the Parliament's Constitutional Committee. Dismissed minister Tamas Suchman compared himself before the committee to a suspect who is informed about the case only after the verdict.
- The government will order a financial investigation presumably in all ministries, with the participation of the Governmental Supervisory Office.

- The opposition party Hungarian Democratic Forum (MDF) said the privatisation scandal may affect further government officials. The Hungarian Democratic People's Party (MDNP) believes the privatisation law has to be amended.
- The Hungarian Association of Trade Union would like to the minimum wage to be raised to 17,500 forints next year.

- There was an explosion yesterday in Budapest in front of 8, Wesselenyi street.The explosive, which was made of gunpowder, blasted in a garbage bin, near the Synagoge, not injuring anybody. The person who placed the bomb is unknown.
